# Invariants (A-B)

<!-- generated by scripts/verify_docs.py --write-nav; do not hand-edit -->

> Code is the source of truth. This file is a map; when it and the code disagree, the code wins.

Every invariant is defined in exactly one file and referenced by id elsewhere.

The index is sharded by family letter: see also [`doctrine/invariants-c-d.md`](invariants-c-d.md), [`doctrine/invariants-e.md`](invariants-e.md), [`doctrine/invariants-f-m.md`](invariants-f-m.md), [`doctrine/invariants-n-pk.md`](invariants-n-pk.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pl-pq.md`](invariants-pl-pq.md), [`doctrine/invariants-pr-r.md`](invariants-pr-r.md), [`doctrine/invariants-s.md`](invariants-s.md), [`doctrine/invariants-t-z.md`](invariants-t-z.md).

| Id | Statement | Defined in |
|---|---|---|
| `INV-AGENT-001` | A role claimed by both a resident and a specialist is refused at boot, when the role registry is built. | [`architecture/agent-taxonomy.md`](../architecture/agent-taxonomy.md) |
| `INV-AGENT-002` | For residents and specialists, `_check_file_set` refuses a missing required file, a forbidden file, or an unrecognised one. | [`architecture/agent-taxonomy.md`](../architecture/agent-taxonomy.md) |
| `INV-AGENT-003` | Specialist loading is isolated per agent and boot-non-fatal; resident loading is not. | [`architecture/agent-taxonomy.md`](../architecture/agent-taxonomy.md) |
| `INV-AGENT-004` | The registry performs no filesystem access; it is an index built from already-loaded configuration. | [`architecture/agent-taxonomy.md`](../architecture/agent-taxonomy.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-004` | A resident-hosted job's session is offered exactly its declaring plugin's tools, `Skill`, `ToolSearch`, the two job tools and its scratchpad — never a delegation, messaging, memory or question tool, and never the resident's own settings, prompt or plugins. | [`architecture/background-jobs.md`](../architecture/background-jobs.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-006` | At most one job per plugin manifest name is live or starting, whichever host kind runs it and whatever the record's shape: `start_job` refuses with `job_busy` while a job record whose qualified job name carries the requested job's manifest name is live or its strict terminal write is still pending, or while another start of that manifest name is inside its pre-record window. | [`architecture/background-job-occupancy.md`](../architecture/background-job-occupancy.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-008` | A specialist's `start_job` starts only a job declared by a plugin assigned to that specialist and loadable when it is called, hosted by that specialist; it is offered only to a delegated turn whose session loads a job-declaring plugin (a tap's pin refuses it, a job or engagement session never holds it), and the job launches with the calling turn's origin — its clearance, chat and resident — at depth 1, under every launch gate a resident's start of that job applies except the delegation ACL and the depth cap. | [`architecture/specialist-job-start.md`](../architecture/specialist-job-start.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-009` | The resident's `<jobs>` listing marks a job as a delegate's own, to be started through a sync text delegation to that delegate, only when that delegate's own `start_job` would accept it at render time; the assistant's served text projection tells it to delegate such a job and that a delegation runs it, and its voice projection that no job starts on a call; it keeps `start_job` for every job it lists; and a specialist's own start returns no engagement id, while the resident's results still carry it. | [`architecture/specialist-job-start.md`](../architecture/specialist-job-start.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-012` | An authenticated operator's reply quoting a post the job record holds, while that record counts as live and is their job in that chat, is delivered into that job as an operator message — ahead of every other route — journaled and admitted synchronously at the seam's entry; it is never sent to another route, and if the job does not take it up its one notice comes from the ticket's holder (INV-ENG-029). | [`architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md`](../architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-013` | A specialist job's question is a filed post whose option buttons carry the engagement id, a random question id redrawn until the record holds no question with it, and the option's index, and whose Cancel button carries the engagement id; job buttons are matched before the generic callback parser; a tap is resolved against the record only — the operator whose job it is, a record that counts as live, a question id it holds and an option it has — and takes the inbound reservation before its first await, so a successful completion is refused from that instant; a question id the record does not hold delivers nothing and answers "This question is no longer active — reply in words". | [`architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md`](../architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-014` | Every in-process terminal winner retires the job's direct-chat keyboards — through the registry's terminal observer, which takes them off the record in one synchronous step before the record leaves the pending-terminal set, or, for a completion from inside a running turn, through that completion's finalize tail once the turn has ended or its bounded wait passed; a keyboard post that lands after the terminal write settled is retired by its filer; and at boot every terminal record still carrying keyboard posts has them retired once. | [`architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md`](../architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-015` | A quiet run that asks the operator something, or receives their reply to one of its posts, a tapped answer or an approval's continuation, stops being quiet before the question is posted or the message is accepted for the job — through a strict write under the registry lock that waits out a pending terminal write and is rolled back, with the interaction refused, when it fails or the record has gone terminal; whether a run's end is told is decided inside its terminal transition from the record's stamp, so an interacting run is told at its end and a run nobody interacted with has its completed end told to no one. | [`architecture/background-job-quiet-runs.md`](../architecture/background-job-quiet-runs.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-016` | A job's session receives Casa's brief once, at launch, and every later input — operator reply, tapped answer, approval continuation, nudge, continue line, restart line — as it arrives, from one writer per job and never held for a turn to end; each write is preceded synchronously by the registry's admission, and the brief and the post-compaction header carry `Started by:` immediately after their first `Job id:` line. | [`architecture/background-job-session.md`](../architecture/background-job-session.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-017` | When a job's turn ends with the record live, no input pending, and no question, approval or parking outstanding since the operator's last input, Casa writes one nudge, and a second such end with no operator input between parks the job — it waits for the operator, who gets one line in their direct chat with Cancel; a turn stopped at the step ceiling is continued if the job reported progress since the previous ceiling and parked otherwise; neither path ends the job, and cost never ends or parks one. | [`architecture/background-job-session.md`](../architecture/background-job-session.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-018` | A job session whose message stream ends while the record is live, other than by Casa's own teardown, is removed from the driver and its client disconnected before a replacement opens, then resumed once with the restart line and every journaled message its transcript lacks; only a failed resume or a second unexpected end ends the job `error`, and then each message the transcript lacks is told as lost once. | [`architecture/background-job-session.md`](../architecture/background-job-session.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-019` | Every job session runs with the long-session auto-compaction window env, the step ceiling and the take-up echo flag, and after a compaction its `SessionStart` hook re-states the job header; any other session start adds nothing. | [`architecture/background-job-session.md`](../architecture/background-job-session.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-020` | A job's cost is recorded at each turn end as its cost before the client opened plus the CLI's cumulative total, persisted, and shown on its end notice; a completion from inside a running turn is torn down only after that turn ends or a bounded wait passes; and no code path reads the cost to stop or refuse anything. | [`architecture/background-job-session.md`](../architecture/background-job-session.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-021` | An operator message is admitted for a job only after its journal entry is committed, and the entry stays until the turn that took it up has ended or it has been told as lost; at boot and at recovery from a session death each entry of a live job is checked against the session transcript by uuid — found means dropped, missing means redelivered once, marked as sent before the restart — and when a job ends, each entry its transcript lacks is told as lost once, at the next boot if Casa died before the job's journal was settled. | [`architecture/background-job-message-journal.md`](../architecture/background-job-message-journal.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-022` | Casa never ends a live job on its own judgement of the work — stopping without finishing, the step ceiling, API faults and cost continue or park it; the job runner ends a job only when its session cannot be resumed after a restart or after its first unexpected end, or ends unexpectedly a second time, and then `error` through the engagement finalize funnel with its reason; every `cancelled` or `error` end of a job appends `Last progress: <summary>` to the text its resident receives, once. | [`architecture/background-jobs.md`](../architecture/background-jobs.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-023` | With no log group configured, a job is started, binds its protected calls to the operator in its origin, asks, takes the operator's replies and taps, and ends with its keyboards retired; neither its launch, its grant identity nor its busy refusal requires a log group. | [`architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md`](../architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-024` | An authenticated operator's reply in their direct chat — text, or a file with a caption — quoting a post filed in that chat by a job they started that no longer counts as live, including a post that landed after the job ended, is, while the tombstone holds the record, the turn of that chat's own agent — the resident in the resident's chat — whose reply note names the job's agent, title, outcome and end time from its record; a reply from anyone else, or in another chat, is that chat's own agent's turn with the ordinary reply note. | [`architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md`](../architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-025` | A run of a job declaring `quietWhenScheduled` that the scheduler started posts nothing in the operator's direct chat except its plugin's delivered slots and Casa's tellings that need the operator — an approval challenge, a cancelled or failed end; a completed end is told to no one and arms no end notification; its agent log is written like any job's; every other run, and every job without the option, is told as before. | [`architecture/background-job-quiet-runs.md`](../architecture/background-job-quiet-runs.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-026` | A job's direct-chat posts — its start line, its questions and its plugin's delivered posts — are filed on its engagement record as they land, without a cap while the record counts as live, persisted, and indexed by address (bot, chat and message id) again at load; a record counts as live while active or idle and while its strict terminal write is pending; the write that settles the terminal transition stores the record's questions empty and keeps its posts, which then leave the live index for the ended-post index keyed by the same address — rebuilt at load from terminal job records, joined by any post of the job that lands after the end, and left by a record pruned from the tombstone. | [`architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md`](../architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md) |
| `INV-BGJOB-027` | A job that its host specialist started on itself from a turn whose `role` is another agent, and that completed, is first handed to that specialist in a delegated turn of its own — at most `MAX_OWNER_PASSES` times along one task — whose answer replaces the job's result in the requester's notice, whose closing message of exactly `<silent/>` sends nothing and clears the owed telling, and whose failure to run or complete, or cancellation, sends the job's own result with the follow-up-failed line; every other job end is told as before, with no such turn. | [`architecture/specialist-job-start.md`](../architecture/specialist-job-start.md) |
| `INV-BRW-001` | Root bootstrap removes the Supervisor token from the s6 container environment on every start, also when bootstrap fails, and writes it to no file or log. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-002` | At most one run is between `starting` and `finishing`; the FIFO lease is taken in one immediate transaction. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-003` | The retention sweep unlinks only paths whose parent directory resolves inside the artifacts directory, and removes a symlink itself, never its target. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-004` | Every `/v1` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <pairing secret>`, except `POST /v1/pair/claim` while the pairing window is open, and every `POST` requires `X-Casa-Browser-Protocol: 1`; both are checked before the route acts. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-005` | A run is queued only when the SHA-256 of the RFC 8785 canonical JSON of the received members other than `admission` equals the admitted digest. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-006` | Exactly one claim inside an armed two-minute window receives the secret, and arming revokes the previous secret and everything issued under it. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-012` | The broker listener admits a request only to a listed 1Password host on port 443 whose `CONNECT` host, TLS server name and `Host` header are the same host. | [`reference/casa-browser-runtime.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runtime.md) |
| `INV-BRW-013` | Chrome starts only as the browser user, only from the launcher, only for a controller-user caller, only with the network floor installed, and always with the Chromium sandbox and a pipe as its only debugging channel. | [`reference/casa-browser-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-016` | A stored file is complete and within its bound; a refused, failed or cancelled transfer leaves no file and no record. | [`reference/casa-browser-files.md`](../reference/casa-browser-files.md) |
| `INV-BRW-019` | No code path in the broker removes a vault item: the broker package uses only the vault facade's read, create and update calls of the 1Password SDK, has no removal, archive or password-generation call and no dynamic attribute access, and forgetting a site changes only the broker's registry. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-022` | A credential is set only on the validated element of a frame whose origin is one of the active site's registered login origins, in the page and generation the driver session is bound to; it never travels as keyboard input. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-023` | While a credential window is open, a proxy event carries only fixed-vocabulary members — its origin only when the run registered it (or it is a fixed extension, broker or infrastructure host), the policy's enums, a normalised method, and keyed binding tags or a callback reference — never request identity, path, query, header or body bytes. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-024` | A session's policy is installed only after the launcher confirmed that no Chrome of the browser user runs; a run takes its intended terminal state, and the next queued run starts, only after its four holds are released — that proof, the proxy's acknowledged revoke of its policy, no driver session left and (an account run) the broker's acknowledged `end_run` — and a run whose release is unconfirmed ends `interrupted`, saying so, while no queued run starts until the release is confirmed. | [`reference/casa-browser-runs.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-025` | A run is never resumed or reinstalled after a restart: a proxy restart, a controller restart and every dependency failure interrupt it, and every install names the proxy start it expects, which a restarted proxy refuses. | [`reference/casa-browser-runs.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-027` | Every driver session the controller opens is closed on every path, and a login or assist live view on an account session exposes the operator's input only after the broker acknowledged its capture (a public-session assist view runs no capture). | [`reference/casa-browser-runs.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-028` | Only a page of the run's public session or the address that served a plain fetch, `https` and at most 800 bytes, gets a source id, and its address leaves the app only through the trusted sources route, except that a plain fetch's own reply states the address that answered it. | [`reference/casa-browser-runs.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-030` | Only Home Assistant's ingress peer reaches the UI — nginx admits that one address and the UI requires a well-formed `X-Ingress-Path` — and every mutation needs a single-use nonce issued for its own path from a same-origin page. | [`reference/casa-browser-ingress.md`](../reference/casa-browser-ingress.md) |
| `INV-BRW-031` | No operator input reaches Chrome before the view's session exists, which is only after the run entered `live` and, on an account session, its manual lease and (login/assist) the broker's capture acknowledgement, nor after any end of the view, which takes effect before anything else is awaited and lets only the operation in flight finish; a page that is no longer the current viewer gets no socket and no input. | [`reference/casa-browser-ingress.md`](../reference/casa-browser-ingress.md) |
| `INV-BRW-032` | A live view returns its run to `running` only after its sockets are closed and every window it resized is back to its earlier bounds, verified with the screen at 1920×1080; a restore that cannot be verified interrupts the run. | [`reference/casa-browser-ingress.md`](../reference/casa-browser-ingress.md) |
| `INV-BRW-034` | A provider binding is shown as bound only when it was learned under the proxy's current binding key; one learned under another key (an HA restore makes a new one) or under no recorded key is shown as needing a live login, and forgetting the site clears it. | [`reference/casa-browser-ingress.md`](../reference/casa-browser-ingress.md) |
| `INV-BRW-036` | An in-scope action runs only after a verdict whose digest is its own frozen packet's; no verdict, a verdict outside the reply bounds, another digest or a stale id runs nothing. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-037` | A tap executes the frozen operation at most once, and only after a `same` re-judgement and a final read identical to the reading it judged. | [`reference/casa-browser-approvals.md`](../reference/casa-browser-approvals.md) |
| `INV-BRW-038` | A question offers a confirm button only when the check stated its facts (`text_incomplete` false), the reading is not blind and, for a money question, the app holds a faithful question screenshot. | [`reference/casa-browser-approvals.md`](../reference/casa-browser-approvals.md) |
| `INV-BRW-039` | A judged press happens only after the target-fact re-read and the hit test pass, immediately before `mouse.down()`; a failure presses nothing. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-040` | In an account session the policy admits a top-level document — or a request whose class the browser did not state — only on the active site's origins and login origins, on a run site's origins or login origins during a live view's manual lease, or as the exact recorded provider binding during the run's login lease. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-041` | In every session, and for every download hop, a request to an address the floor refuses is refused, Chrome's own background sends to its background hosts are refused, and a fixed exception — an infrastructure rule or the provider binding — admits a request only within its declared shape. | [`reference/casa-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-042` | On the browser and download listeners no byte reaches an upstream for a request the current policy refuses — an account session's off-site top-level document included, while its pages' other requests reach any floor-checked origin — the proxy dials only an address the floor checked for that host (never a name resolved outside a decision), and once a policy change is acknowledged no request or WebSocket frame admitted under the earlier policy is sent, except that `end_login` and `end_manual` leave in flight what the policy after them admits when no lease has admitted anything the policy without leases refuses since the last close of every connection, and an `install` that only adds provider bindings leaves everything in flight. | [`reference/casa-browser-runtime.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runtime.md) |
| `INV-BRW-043` | An observation or a screenshot is produced only when the page-view gate admits the page's full current address as the session's own — in an account session, the site's origins or login origins; in the public session, an address the floor admits — before and after it is read, and an observation carries no address beyond an origin, no selector, no attribute but the name of an element with no visible one (a button input's value, `aria-label`, `title`, `alt`), no other field's value as a name, and no value of a field the one secret rule recognises — a password, one-time-code or payment-card field, as the field is when it is read — each field whose value it shows being asked that rule again right after the reading. | [`reference/casa-browser-observations.md`](../reference/casa-browser-observations.md) |
| `INV-BRW-044` | In an account run a navigation to an address off the run's account sites is sent only from the public session, after the account browser closed; a top-level navigation the run's leases-free policy refuses is never sent and is answered `blocked`; and the model never types into a password field. | [`reference/casa-browser-runs.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runs.md) |
| `INV-BRW-045` | A download hop the run's policy refuses as a download hop is never sent; a hop it admits is decided again by the enforcing proxy on its download listener, which alone admits it to the upstream, and an account cookie is attached only to a hop whose origin is the link's page's or the active account site's. | [`reference/casa-browser-files.md`](../reference/casa-browser-files.md) |
| `INV-BRW-046` | A public link download whose detected type is outside the document set is recorded only when a go verdict or an executed confirmation for its own pending judgement keeps it, and at any other end of that judgement its bytes are deleted. | [`reference/casa-browser-files.md`](../reference/casa-browser-files.md) |
| `INV-BRW-047` | Each service user can open only its one permitted route — the browser user the proxy's browser listener, the controller user the proxy's download listener, the broker user the proxy's broker listener, the proxy user public TCP and the configured resolver, the VNC user none, the ingress user only replies on its port — and no service starts unless root init installed that floor. | [`reference/casa-browser-runtime.md`](../reference/casa-browser-runtime.md) |
| `INV-BRW-048` | A live-view credential is written only from the capture's last attempt that the check judged `signed_in`, that did not fail, with no password typing after it, ending on one of the site's origins; it overwrites a linked item only when that item is `unverified` or its own password was rejected in this run, and never writes equal values. | [`reference/casa-browser-signin.md`](../reference/casa-browser-signin.md) |
| `INV-BRW-049` | The broker never changes a credential on its own: a page offering a new-password field during a login ends that login for the live view before anything is filled, and a captured value reaches the vault only through a live-view sign-in the check judged signed in (INV-BRW-048). | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-050` | Forgetting a site's login removes only its item link: the site stays registered with its login origins, no vault call is made, and its next login asks the operator again. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-051` | A site's sign-in code is filled only into the one code field of the very document that reported `needs_code` (the same page generation and the mark the report set in that document, on a login origin, with exactly that field and a submit), once per report, through a fresh login driver session closed on every path; it never appears in a broker or API reply, an error, the run's events, the broker's journal or registry, the app's records, or a log line. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-052` | A line break an agent types reaches only a real `<textarea>`, never with Enter after it, and only as inserted text, never as a key. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-053` | A site is registered from a sign-in card only by the operator's Yes on that card, for exactly the origin the card showed (read from the browser, never from the model), and a card never signs in to a registered site that reaches more than that origin. | [`reference/casa-browser-signin.md`](../reference/casa-browser-signin.md) |
| `INV-BRW-054` | Only `confirm` can execute a question's frozen operation: `not_now` declines and an extra option answers, neither pressing anything, and a tap on a question that is no longer current (another revision or digest, lapsed, expired) executes nothing. | [`reference/casa-browser-approvals.md`](../reference/casa-browser-approvals.md) |
| `INV-BRW-055` | What the probe reads goes only to the current viewer — never to a log, a model or any other surface; it holds a password field's length, never its value. | [`reference/casa-browser-ingress.md`](../reference/casa-browser-ingress.md) |
| `INV-BRW-056` | An automatic sign-in whose page changed under a step reads the page again from settling before any further value is set, and only while every frame holding one of the step's live handles has kept, throughout, the address origin it had when the handle was issued and stayed attached (otherwise it refuses); it reports `logged_in` only after a submit of its own — a read with no fields after the step's fields were found is `page_unsettled`, and a sign-in that filled nothing and found no form is `no_form`. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-057` | The 1Password guest's email, Secret Key and password are set only into the main frame of the guest session's own tab, and only while that document is exactly `https://my.1password.<region>/signin` (sign-in) or the extension's popup page (unlock), checked in the same evaluation that sets the value. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-058` | An automatic sign-in answers a passkey prompt only through 1Password's notification frame of the login page itself, on a login origin, when the prompt offers exactly the site's linked item (its username, and its title, which names no other login in the vault once trimmed), at most once per run and site, and a sign-in that answered it — continued with a code or not — claims nothing (`no_form`). | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-059` | Off the start page, Casa Browser fills or presses nothing of a sign-in without a `sign_in` verdict on that page, only fields of the judged reading (a field the page does not mark only as the verdict mapped it, a password only into a password field), and only while the documents, fields, buttons, labels and destinations it judged are unchanged and no step came between; a look sends the password once, answers only its judged page's passkey, and signs in again only after a sign-in of the run that worked. | [`reference/casa-browser-signin.md`](../reference/casa-browser-signin.md) |
| `INV-BRW-060` | An automatic sign-in sends the password at most once per sign-in, and never while a shown, editable, empty box of its form stays unfilled: the read and the click's own evaluation both check it, and a form that asks again goes to the live view. | [`reference/casa-browser-credentials.md`](../reference/casa-browser-credentials.md) |
| `INV-BRW-061` | A picture for a model comes only from the one capture rule (password, one-time-code and payment-card fields and every child frame black), is held in memory only for its judgement or its one reply, and reaches no store row, stored response or file; with no picture a judgement is the same text check. | [`reference/casa-browser-observations.md`](../reference/casa-browser-observations.md) |
| `INV-BRW-062` | A `go` on `account_change` runs only on a packet carrying `approved`; `approved` is set only by an executed confirm on a question that showed the plan, and is absent on another site and on a page with a card field; such a `go` presses only while what its packet was built from is unchanged; `payment` and `commitment` always ask. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-063` | Apart from `scroll` and a same-host navigation (INV-BRW-065), an action on a signed-in site that runs with no check is only typing without Enter, a select's value, or a click on a non-secret checkbox, radio, `summary` or `aria-expanded` button with no link or submitter destination; a press or Enter that sends after it is judged on a reading holding every tick and value it made; an action marked `ask_first` never runs with no check. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-064` | A plain fetch carries no cookie, whatever the session or destination, sends no hop the policy or the floor refuses, and neither reads nor changes Chrome, the session or the installed policy; only its own answer keeps addresses whole, and a file downloaded or captured from a page stays fully masked. | [`reference/casa-browser-files.md`](../reference/casa-browser-files.md) |
| `INV-BRW-065` | On an account session a navigation to a site with account access runs with no check only when the destination has the hostname of the web page open now and belongs to this session's own site, the step carries no plan, and it is not the open page's own address with a fragment; those facts are asked again just before the load, and every click on a link to such a site is checked. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
| `INV-BRW-066` | Past a reading's control cap a stable page's confirm presses however it was scrolled, and a change in any comparable control, listed or not, in any shown frame, or in the text of the target's own record, stops the press. | [`reference/casa-browser-approvals.md`](../reference/casa-browser-approvals.md) |
| `INV-BRW-067` | An observation's `find` searches every actionable control of the page, past the cap, and says no control holds the words only when the search was whole, a closed shadow root in any frame's document ruling that out; its words never enter the page and it matches only the masked text a reply shows, never a secret field's value or a secret select's options, so what masking hides changes no part of the reply; and it changes neither what `gate.py::READ` lists nor its digest. | [`reference/casa-browser-observations.md`](../reference/casa-browser-observations.md) |
| `INV-BRW-068` | A repeated `scroll` on one handle advances instead of going back to its element, the first brings that element into view, and every scroll's reply states how far down of how far in all, and whether it moved. | [`reference/casa-browser-browser.md`](../reference/casa-browser-browser.md) |
| `INV-BRW-069` | A packet shows every field's value whole and masked, never cut: in `target.form.fields` when the target's form lists that field, else in the field's `page.controls` line (a typed target repeats its own value in the action and its state); a field of another frame is never taken for one of the target's form. | [`reference/casa-browser-actions.md`](../reference/casa-browser-actions.md) |
